subject: Request: strategic snapback credit for Elixir Health – VP/CFO signoff needed
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@elixirhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Final pricing request for planned pilot + route to production

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the routing controls. We want to move forward with a 3-month pilot and a production roll in Q4, but procurement needs a clear commercial concession to get the board approval.

Quick ask from their side: a 35% blended platform discount for the first 6 months (pilot + ramp), plus a credit for any missed latency SLOs during onboarding. Committed ARR target if we convert: $1.2M in year one.

I know this is a meaningful request. Can your team share what exceptions or limited-time credits you can offer? We can sign a short SOW and include a rollback clause if performance doesn't meet the pilot KPIs.

Attached: draft SOW (Elixir_SOW_v1.pdf) — procurement wants the numbers in the SOW.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Cloud Integrations, Elixir Health
elena.ruiz@elixirhealth.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Final pricing request for planned pilot + route to production

Forwarding Elixir's ask. Key facts: planned 3-month pilot, potential $1.2M ARR if converted, external asks 35% blended discount first 6 months + latency-credit. Attached SOW and our discount matrix (redwood_discount_matrix.xlsx).

My read: we can do a constrained concession but 35% up-front across the board is outside our standard guardrails for this deal size and the infrastructure profile (multi-region with dedicated instances). Proposed structure (recommendation):
- Offer a 30% 'introductory snapback credit' applied to invoices for first 90 days only, recoverable if usage exceeds 1.5x forecast in month 4–6 (i.e., credit snaps back to zero).
- Follow with a 15% volume discount months 4–6 if they meet committed ARR ramp milestones.
- Include clearly defined latency SLO credit language limited to onboarding (max credit cap $25k).
- Require written pilot KPIs and a 60-day notice to terminate the concession.

Financial impact: estimated 3-month revenue reduction ~$45k (gross) but protectable by snapback. Upside: high probability to convert to $1.2M ARR.

Can you run quick margin math and confirm we can sign this as an exception with VP/CFO signoff? If yes, I will prepare a one-page exception memo for Marissa.

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Final pricing request for planned pilot + route to production

Naomi —
Short note: the proposed snapback structure is sensible operationally and limits downside. Quick calc using conservative usage projections: 30% snapback for 3 months = ~$48k reduction at our midpoint scenario; net present value over year 1 of conversion still positive (>$880k).

Flag: enterprise procurement will expect the structure codified in SOW and likely push on 'snapback recovery' language. Please escalate to Marissa for VP/CFO approval — I won't sign without explicit finance signoff.

+1 to attaching a recovery cap and a hard stop on credits after 180 days.
Jonas
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Exception memo: approve limited 'snapback' credit for Elixir Health (ELX-2027-04)

Marissa —
Following up with a short exception memo for VP/CFO review. Context, ask, and recommended guardrails below. Elixir is a strategic prospect in diagnostics with a platform integration complexity that benefits from our dedicated routing and latency guarantees. Probability to convert after pilot is high.

Rationale:
- Commercial: potential FY1 ARR $1.2M with an expected 40% gross margin on steady-state usage; pilot is a low friction path to a large program.
- Competitive: competing vendors are offering deeper up-front discounts; we risk losing position without a short, conditional concession.
- Operational: the pilot increases utilization on east/west dedicated pools for months 7–9, improving long-term efficiency.

Recommended concession (terms to include in SOW):
1) "Introductory snapback credit": 30% credit applied to platform invoices for months 1–3 of the engagement (pilot + immediate ramp). Credits are invoices-level adjustments, not prepaid cash.
2) Performance ramp discount: 15% discount months 4–6 only if usage meets committed ramp milestones documented in Appendix A.
3) Snapback recovery: if cumulative usage in months 4–6 exceeds 1.5x forecast, credits applied in months 1–3 will be recouped via a true-up on the month 7 invoice (no retroactive cash demands; recovery limited to credited amount).
4) Latency SLO credit: onboarding SLA credit capped at $25,000, only claimable for verified SLO misses during pilot window.
5) Credit cap: total credits/adjustments capped at $75,000.
6) End date and notice: concession expires after 180 days; requires 60 days notice for termination.

Financial impact (mid-case):
- Estimated gross revenue reduction in first 3 months: ~$48,000 per our margin model.
- Upside: expected conversion value ~$1.2M ARR; NPV >$800k with conservative retention assumptions.

Risk mitigations:
- Recovery clause (snapback).
- Credit cap and latency SLO verification process.
- Legal to include explicit KPI appendix and acceptance criteria.

Attachments: Elixir_SOW_v1.pdf, redwood_discount_matrix.xlsx.

Ask: Approve this exception for a one-time concession tied to deal ELX-2027-04. If approved, I will update the SOW language and route to procurement/Elena for signature.

Thanks for reviewing — I appreciate a quick hit given procurement timelines.

— Naomi
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception memo: approve limited 'snapback' credit for Elixir Health (ELX-2027-04)

Naomi —
Reviewed the memo and the attached discount matrix. I approve the one-time exception under the conditions you outlined. Conditions for sign-off:
1) Legal drafts explicit KPI appendix and a clear recovery true-up clause (no ambiguity on measurement or timing).
2) Credit cap set to $75,000 in the SOW (no increase).
3) Finance to receive monthly usage reports months 1–7 for verification; Jonas to confirm cadence.
4) Product commit: engineering will prioritize onboarding for a single east-coast routing cluster (confirm with ops).

Once Legal confirms amended SOW language, Finance will countersign the exception and Naomi you may proceed to execute SOW with the Elixir procurement contact.

Marissa Cole
VP, Finance (Interim CFO authority)
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
